name: Solenne Neuralcrest Port Fascinator
description:
A sculptural fascinator mounted on a low-profile chromium headband, designed to frame and aestheticize exposed BCI port hardware as a deliberate style statement. The piece is constructed from hand-formed biosync resin petals — translucent and faintly bioluminescent in warm amber — arranged in an asymmetric crest that rises from the left temple. Embedded microfilaments pulse in slow rhythmic patterns synchronized to the wearer's neural activity via a passive BCI tap.

The mounting bracket precisely accommodates four-port and six-port cranial configurations. Available in bespoke fits only. Each piece is signed by a Solenne artisan inside the headband.
functionality: Passive BCI tap syncs bioluminescent pulse pattern to wearer's real-time neural activity — calm states produce slow amber waves, heightened states produce rapid gold flickers. The headband bracket protects port hardware while displaying it as a luxury feature. Custom-fitted to individual cranial and port geometry.
what_it_says: Your augmentation is not a utility — it is art, and you paid to make that unmistakably clear.
story_hooks: The passive BCI tap in a Solenne fascinator was found to be logging neural pattern data and transmitting it to an unknown off-site receiver — the wearer had been broadcasting their emotional state through every Spire event for two years.
A fascinator commissioned for a now-disgraced executive was quietly resold through a Tier 3 broker — it still syncs to the original owner's neural signature, flickering erratically on any new wearer.
A Spire heir's fascinator pulsed in a distress pattern for six seconds during a live broadcast before returning to normal — analysts who know the code are divided on what it means.
